BiblicalUsage: Kedorlaomer was the king of Elam who ruled the cities of the plain: Genesis 14:1 names him with Amraphel and Arioch and Tidal, the kings of the east. Genesis 14:4 says twelve years they served Chedorlaomer, and in the thirteenth year they rebelled. Genesis 14:5 says in the fourteenth year came Chedorlaomer, and the kings that were with him, and smote the Rephaims.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Chedorlaomer is the picture of every power that taxes God's people until Abraham rises to take them back.
